prompt: What question does code coverage answer exactly?

choices.text: Whether the tests are good enough to ship
choices.why: That is the question it cannot answer.

choices.text: Which code no test executed
choices.why: Right. It records what ran, and so what did not.

choices.text: How many bugs remain in the code
choices.why: Coverage counts lines, not bugs.

choices.text: How fast each test runs
choices.why: That is --durations, from lesson 1.

prompt: What total coverage did shipquote's full suite reach at step 7?
Why was carrier.py at 66%, with all of CarrierClient missing?

choices.text: Because CarrierClient is dead code nobody calls
choices.why: production calls it through price.

choices.text: Because coverage cannot measure network code
choices.why: It measures any Python that runs in the process.

choices.text: Its only tests, the contract tests, were skipped
choices.why: Right. CARRIER_URL was not set, so the two ss in the progress line became missing lines.

choices.text: Because the stub tests replaced it with a mock
choices.why: The stubs replace the carrier passed to price; CarrierClient is a separate class.

prompt: A suite starts the server with subprocess and sends it a hundred requests. What will coverage report for app.py, measured the usual way?

choices.text: Little or nothing
choices.why: Right. Only the measured process counts, unless the subprocess is measured too.

choices.text: 100%, since every route was requested
choices.why: The requests ran code in a process coverage was not watching.

choices.text: The same as the in-thread functional tests
choices.why: Threads are in the process; a subprocess is not.

choices.text: An error, since coverage refuses subprocesses
choices.why: It runs; it simply does not see them.

prompt: Running only the after-two and Friday dispatch tests, line coverage said 100%. What did branch coverage add?

choices.text: Nothing; it also said 100%
choices.why: It said 94%.

choices.text: The arc 13->15
choices.why: Right. Both orders were after 14:00, so the decision always went the same way.

choices.text: Line 16, the weekend loop
choices.why: Line 16 ran for the Friday order.

choices.text: A warning that two tests were deselected
choices.why: That came from pytest, not coverage.

prompt: What percentage did branch coverage give dispatch.py in that run?
No test formats a negative price, yet brl's line with the conditional expression shows as covered under branch coverage. Why?

choices.text: Because branch coverage counts only if statements in functions with docstrings
choices.why: There is no such rule.

choices.text: Because a negative price is impossible
choices.why: brl handles one; it is simply never tested.

choices.text: Because show_missing is on
choices.why: That only lists missing lines.

choices.text: Branch coverage measures jumps between lines, and the decision is inside one
choices.why: Right. Conditional expressions and short-circuits hide within a line.

prompt: Coverage turns branch measurement on with the setting branch = ___ .
The file of tests with no assertions reached 100% of money.py. Then brl was broken. What happened?

choices.text: Coverage dropped below 100%
choices.why: The same lines ran.

choices.text: Both tests failed
choices.why: They assert nothing, so nothing could fail them.

choices.text: Both still passed
choices.why: Right. Covered means ran, not checked.

choices.text: pytest warned about tests without asserts
choices.why: pytest gives no such warning.

prompt: Which of these count as covered exactly like a careful test? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A test that checks the status code and not the body
choices.why: Right. Every line it ran counts.

choices.text: A call made in setup and never checked
choices.why: Right. Setup lines count as executed.

choices.text: An assertion that a result is not None
choices.why: Right. The code ran; the check is weak.

choices.text: A test that was skipped
choices.why: A skipped test runs nothing, so it covers nothing.

prompt: Which half of the coverage report cannot mislead you?

choices.text: The list of lines that never ran
choices.why: Right. A line that never ran is a line no test checked.

choices.text: The total percentage
choices.why: The total counts weak tests like strong ones.

choices.text: The files at 100%
choices.why: money.py reached 100% with no assertions.

choices.text: The number of statements per file
choices.why: That describes the code, not the tests.

prompt: In mutation testing, what does it mean that a mutant survived?

choices.text: The mutated code crashed on import
choices.why: A crash would fail the suite, which kills the mutant.

choices.text: No test noticed the change
choices.why: Right. The suite cannot tell the mutant from the real code.

choices.text: The mutation was undone before the run
choices.why: The script restores the file after the run.

choices.text: Coverage of that file dropped
choices.why: Mutation testing does not measure coverage.

prompt: How many of the eight mutants did shipquote's suite kill?
Why did dropping id DESC from the store's ORDER BY survive?

choices.text: Because SQLite ignores the second sort key
choices.why: It does not; ties are what it decides.

choices.text: Because store.py is excluded from the run
choices.why: store.py ran and was 100% covered.

choices.text: No test has a tie
choices.why: Right. The factory keeps timestamps distinct, so the tie-break is never exercised.

choices.text: Because the -x flag stopped the run early
choices.why: -x stops at the first failure, and there was none.

prompt: store.py shows 100% coverage and two surviving mutants. What do the survivors call for?

choices.text: More lines executed in store.py
choices.why: Every line already ran.

choices.text: New assertions
choices.why: Right. They are assertion problems, invisible to coverage.

choices.text: Excluding store.py from mutation runs
choices.why: That hides the finding.

choices.text: A higher fail_under
choices.why: The threshold is about coverage, which is already full.

prompt: Match each tool to its language.
coverage report --fail-under=85 | tail -1 printed the failure and then exit status 0. Why 0?

choices.text: Because 81 rounds up to 85
choices.why: Coverage printed that 81 is less than 85.

choices.text: The status shown was tail's
choices.why: Right. A pipeline's status is its last command's by default.

choices.text: Because --fail-under only warns
choices.why: Without the pipe it exited 2.

choices.text: Because the report was empty
choices.why: It printed the total and the failure.

prompt: Two tests that checked nothing raised the total from 81% to what?
Which gate does the lesson describe as a ratchet?

choices.text: Failing below a fixed percentage chosen by the team
choices.why: That is the plain threshold.

choices.text: Failing when a change's own lines are not covered
choices.why: That is coverage of the change.

choices.text: Failing only if coverage drops below main's
choices.why: Right. It can stay or rise, never fall.

choices.text: Failing when a mutant survives
choices.why: That is a mutation gate.

prompt: When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure: that is ___ 's law.
The heavy-parcel surcharge moved the total from 81% to 80%. What did the file report add?

choices.text: That the surcharge was fully tested
choices.why: No test sends a parcel over 30 kg.

choices.text: That line 30, the new return, never ran
choices.why: Right. The if ran for every quote; the new behaviour never did.

choices.text: That the change broke the free-shipping rule
choices.why: All 41 tests still passed.

choices.text: Nothing; the file was still at 100%
choices.why: It dropped to 93%.

prompt: Why does a gate on the lines a change added suit a pull request better than a gate on the total?

choices.text: Because it cannot be met by tests that check nothing
choices.why: It can; every coverage gate shares that weakness.

choices.text: Because it runs faster than a full report
choices.why: Speed is not the argument.

choices.text: It asks about the author's own change
choices.why: Right. And it cannot be met by adding a test elsewhere.

choices.text: Because the total never changes
choices.why: It moved from 81% to 80% here.

prompt: A tool that reads a coverage report and a git diff and prints the uncovered changed lines is called diff-___ .
Why does shipquote exclude the __main__ guard but keep main() counted?

choices.text: main() holds things worth checking
choices.why: Right. The smoke test of lesson 7 will check it; excluding it would hide that nothing does yet.

choices.text: Because coverage cannot exclude functions
choices.why: It can, with a pattern or a pragma.

choices.text: Because main() is already fully covered
choices.why: Lines 60 to 63 are missing.

choices.text: Because the guard is slower to test
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

prompt: Which of these deserves an exclusion, by the lesson's table?

choices.text: Error handling you have not tested yet
choices.why: That is a test to write.

choices.text: A whole module that is hard to test
choices.why: Hard is a reason to look, not to hide.

choices.text: Code under if TYPE_CHECKING:
choices.why: Right. It exists for type checkers and never runs.

choices.text: A branch you believe cannot happen
choices.why: Belief is what a test checks.

prompt: With the guard excluded, what did app.py's coverage become?
The two layers were measured separately with -p and combined. What total did the combined report show?

choices.text: The fast layer's total alone
choices.why: Combine merges both files.

choices.text: The average of the two runs
choices.why: Coverage is a union of lines, not an average.

choices.text: 81%, the same as one full run
choices.why: Right. The union of the two runs is the whole suite.

choices.text: 100%, since every test ran once
choices.why: Lines the suite never reaches stay missing.

prompt: Put the pipeline steps for combined coverage in order.
items: Each test job runs coverage run -p
Each job keeps its data file as an artifact
A final job downloads the artifacts
The final job runs coverage combine and report
trap: Combining comes after every artifact is downloaded, in one job that runs last.

prompt: Why should the combined report be produced even when a test job failed?

choices.text: Because coverage fails the build on its own
choices.why: That is a separate gate.

choices.text: A failure is when the report is wanted most
choices.why: Right. Skipping it removes the report from the moment it is most useful.

choices.text: Because coverage combine deletes the artifacts
choices.why: It merges files; deleting them is not the point.

choices.text: To raise the total above the threshold
choices.why: The report changes nothing about the total.

prompt: What percentage of statements did go test -cover report for internal/grade?
Why did the capture use -count=1 with go test?

choices.text: To run each test only once instead of three times
choices.why: go test runs each test once by default.

choices.text: To skip the cached result
choices.why: Right. Without it, an unchanged package prints (cached).

choices.text: To turn coverage on
choices.why: -cover turns coverage on.

choices.text: To stop at the first failing package
choices.why: That is -failfast, and only within a package.

prompt: A Java team reports 85% from JaCoCo and a Python team 78% from coverage.py. What does the lesson say about comparing them?

choices.text: The Java team tests more carefully
choices.why: The numbers count different units and say nothing about care.

choices.text: The Python team should raise its threshold to 85%
choices.why: A target invites the gaming of section 06.

choices.text: Compare each with itself over time
choices.why: Right. The tools count different things; the missing list is what to read.

choices.text: Add the two and divide by two
choices.why: An average of different units is meaningless.

prompt: Match each finding to the tool that produced it.

pairs.left: line 30 of the surcharge never ran

prompt: A manager asks for 95% coverage by the end of the quarter. Which response follows this course?

choices.text: Agree, and add tests for every uncovered line
choices.why: That is the target that gets met by tests checking nothing.

choices.text: Propose a gate on changed lines instead
choices.why: Right. Coverage stays a diagnostic; tests are added for failures you can name.

choices.text: Exclude the hard files so the total reaches 95%
choices.why: That is the same game played with configuration.

choices.text: Refuse to measure coverage at all
choices.why: The missing list is valuable; the course keeps it.

prompt: Which of these did shipquote's coverage report reveal at step 7? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The SMTP mailer's real code never runs in a test
choices.why: Right. mailer.py was at 36%.

choices.text: The carrier client's contract tests were skipped
choices.why: Right. carrier.py lost all of CarrierClient.

choices.text: The store's tie-break is never checked
choices.why: That came from mutation testing; coverage showed store.py at 100%.

choices.text: The /version route was never requested
choices.why: Right. Lines 20 and 21 of app.py were missing.
